captured_note: SigLIP appears in the capture's Step-3 CompEval (multimodal) evaluation as an as-is comparison: the official sigmoid-loss image-text pretrained image tower is downloaded and a linear probe is fit on its frozen pooled image embedding, because the from-scratch pretraining (the WebLI image-text corpus, many TPU-days) is not reproduced. This port carries that as-is comparison only. There is NO author submodule: the SigLIP model class is timm's (a pinned pip dependency, timm==1.0.28), imported not copied, and the weights are a sha256-pinned download.

paper.title: Sigmoid Loss for Language Image Pre-Training

note: Eval-only port (a single linear_eval stage, no pretraining). The backbone is timm's vit_base_patch16_siglip_224.webli (the SigLIP image tower, no class token, a MAP attention-pool head), built with pretrained=False and the sha256-pinned checkpoint (backbone_artifact below) loaded into it. Because the source is a pip dependency and not a git submodule, this file records NO upstream block and the adapter defines no UPSTREAM (test_port_completeness's both-places rule requires them to agree, and here both are absent).
linear_eval: Probes SigLIP's pooled pre-classifier image embedding (timm model built with num_classes=0), frozen. SigLIP's image-text pretraining yields a genuine learned representation, so the number is comparable (the multimodal 'pretrained-backbone reuse' row, the SigLIP sibling of 38_clip). A real run needs the official checkpoint (backbone_artifact below, fetched and hash-verified by bin/fetch-weights.py --artifact backbone_artifact, passed as the config's train.ckpt); the hermetic smoke leaves ckpt empty and builds a random tiny SigLIP-style ViT, so nothing is downloaded and only the pipeline is exercised. See docs/EVAL_DOWNLOAD.md.

backbone_artifact.name: ViT-B/16 SigLIP 224px image tower (timm)
backbone_artifact.sha256_source: read on 2026-08-27 from the HuggingFace LFS metadata (https://huggingface.co/api/models/timm/vit_base_patch16_siglip_224.webli/paths-info/main, lfs.oid for pytorch_model.bin at revision 8db107e594ed7552e44e108f16650d81ac6de9a6); bin/fetch-weights.py re-verifies this value on download

rewritten_during_the_port: the model class is timm's, not a copied or submoduled author repository; the pretrained weights are a sha256-pinned HuggingFace download (backbone_artifact) rather than a timm pretrained=True auto-download, so CI never fetches and a real run is hash-verified
the device is resolved (resolve_device) instead of assumed CUDA
features are extracted in fp32 (no autocast), so the frozen-feature probe runs identically on a CPU or a pre-Ampere GPU

the probe follows this port's shared frozen-backbone protocol (mean-centre + L2-normalise, a single linear layer with SGD + cosine), returning the four comparable linear-probe accuracies and the epoch count

the input normalisation is taken from the backbone's own timm data config (SigLIP uses a symmetric 0.5 mean/std, not ImageNet's); the crop resolution is read from the config so the hermetic smoke can shrink it and build a random tiny SigLIP-style VisionTransformer (no class token, a MAP attention-pool head) instead of the full ViT-B/16
